long_description:
## The world is a lot right now. This is time to slow down, support our nervous systems, and practice co-regulation together in community.

Chair Yoga offers a gentle, accessible chair-based movement and meditation practice. Using chairs for support, we’ll move slowly, breathe together, and take time to settle — no mats, no experience, no expectations.

Chairs are provided; All abilities are welcome and encouraged to join. Yoga mats are NOT necessary!

The entire practice can take place seated on the chair, with a few options for using the chair for balance in standing variations of poses.

While this is a public class and not specifically an LGBTQ+ event, you'll be supported by a queer yoga teacher <3

This class will be led by elle brodsky, founder of Rainbow Fit Club and certified yoga teacher since 2008.

description: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening Classes will guide you through complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual wisdom. Our weekly live Zoom classes will guide you through the complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual knowledge. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue between Krishna (the teacher) and Arjuna (the student), addresses life's deepest questions: What is the nature of the Self? What is the highest purpose of existence? How can one live with intelligence and clarity? If all existence is One, why do we perceive differences? What is the nature of the universe and its origin? How can we understand the cause of the universe? How does one transcend the sense of limitation? This comprehensive study covers: The nature of the Self (Atman) and Reality (Brahman) Self-knowledge that includes dozens of methods to reveal your nature The role of karma, dharma, and free will The nature of the mind and consciousness (or awareness) The art of wise living and decision-making Cultivating emotional maturity and inner peace Through this course, you will: Grasp the core teachings of the Bhagavad Gita and their relevance to modern life Apply practical techniques for refining your thinking and mastering your emotions Develop a deeper understanding of your identity and the world Cultivate inner peace, clarity, and purpose This knowledge offers a step-by-step method to liberate the seeker from the confines of the ego, from the limitations imposed by the material world, and from the cycle of rebirth. Registration is open for our fall HEALING WITH MANTRAS kirtan retreat at @kripalucenter October 9 - 12, 2026. These dates fill up quickly (it's Indigenous People's Day /Columbus Day weekend!) so reserve your spots early! 

In this program, we'll learn and practice healing mantras from the Tibetan Buddhist and Tibetan medical traditions and experience their effects on our minds, our chakras, our hearts, and the energy channels of the subtle body.

📿 In the mornings, we'll practice simple mantra recitation (speech-level spoken chants) and silent chanting (inner-voice chanting) to activate healing energies and quell inner and secret obstacles. 

🎶 In the afternoons and select evenings, we'll practice kirtan (call-and-response chanting) and sing devotional mantras from the Buddhist and Hindu traditions.

This retreat is an opportunity to learn and practice deep rest and deep self-care. 

You will:

- learn how to use your own voice and sound currents to heal your own body, voice, and mind. 💫

- immerse in the profound beauty of the Kripalu campus, nestled in the Berkshire Mountains, and enjoy trail hikes, boating, and guided outdoor activities at peak foliage season. And nature, as we know, is good medicine. 🌈

- Enjoy world-class food (based on Ayurvedic principles), Ayurvedic spa treatments, and a wide array of yoga/meditation/dance/art classes to choose from. 🔥

- enjoy the company of supportive and like-minded community who are committed to being of benefit to all beings 

- Receive guidance and instruction for home practice.

description: Experience the Vibrancy of Bengali Culture at Rishi Panda Live Concert & PBA Durga pujo 2026
long_description:
Experience the Vibrancy of Bengali Culture at Rishi Panda Live Concert & PBA Durga pujo 2026
Mark your calendars for the 11th of October, 2026, as the Rishi Panda Live Concert & PBA Durga Pujo 2026 in NJ is set to make waves. Hosted by the Princeton Bengali Association (princetonbengalees), this anticipated event will be a marvelous blend of music, spirituality, food, and drink. Immerse yourself in the multilingual performances, witness the vibrancy of Bengali and Hindi cultural traditions, and enjoy a live concert that is sure to leave you spellbound.
Unveiling the Talent of Rishi Panda
At the heart of this event is the acclaimed independent artist, Rishi Panda. From his humble beginnings as a young music enthusiast, Rishi has grown into a popular YouTuber and singer. His partnership with JMR Music has given birth to a plethora of captivating original and cover songs. Known for his soul-stirring performances, Rishi Panda will undoubtedly enchant the audience at this concert.
Discover the Charm of Community Middle School
The event will take place at the well-known Community Middle School, located at 95 Grovers Mill Rd, in the picturesque city of Plainsboro, NJ, United States. The venue is known for its safety and easy accessibility, enhancing the overall experience for attendees. Additionally, the area boasts numerous Indian restaurants for those looking to indulge in authentic Indian cuisine after the event. Parking facilities will also be available at the venue, ensuring convenience for all attendees.
Choose Your Perfect Ticket
Various ticket options are available to cater to your needs. For adults over 12 years, non-veg and veg options are priced at $65.00. For kids aged between 5 and 12 years, comprehensive tickets are available at $55.00. For those who wish to attend only the Rishi Panda show, tickets for adults are priced at $50.00, and for kids, at $45.00. Children below 5 years can enjoy the event at no cost. Secure your spot today to experience an unforgettable celebration of Bengali culture and music.

I bet you haven’t laughed like this in months and will feel lighter afterward!
Join us for a fun and rejuvenating session of Laughter Yoga at the Shelley Lake Fishing Pier's top seating area! This event is all about spreading positivity and laughter through simple scream therapy, deep breathing exercises, Laughter Yoga, clapping, stomping, shaking, and playful activities. title: Yoga for a Cause - benefitting Voices for Parkinson's
description: Join us for an all-levels yoga class to benefit the mission of Voices for Parkinson's
long_description:
Join us for an all-levels yoga class to benefit the mission of Voices for Parkinson's

About this Event

Come flow with us to benefit. Voices For Parkinson's provides in-person and telehealth speech therapy services for residents of Ohio. Individual, 1:1 services are currently provided at Alpha Neuro Fitness (800 E Ross Ave) in Cincinnati, OH. Weekly speech maintenance groups are offered via a hybrid approach, with the option for virtual and/or in-person attendance. The nonprofit organization offers a whole-person approach to treating the symptoms of Parkinson's disease, relating to problems with cognition, voice, and swallowing. We offer resources and education, and collaborate with an interdisciplinary team including local businesses to provide the most up-to-date information to our clients and their community.
100% of all donations go directly to the charity. We thank Fretboard Brewing for donating the space and Anissa Dowling for donating her time and talent in leading the yoga class that is always fun and perfect for all levels.
Bring a friend and enjoy $1 off beers in the tap room after class!

Yoga Nidra is a guided meditation that will lead you to the deepest level of relaxation. This technique brings your body, mind and soul in direct communion with your energy body. It allows for Prana, Life Energy, to heal areas that need attention. By quieting the thoughts in your mind, you tap into the ability to heal innately. long_description:
Teaching Yoga through a Trauma-Informed Lens - 8 hour training for yoga teachers

TUESDAY | OCT 13 | 6:00-8:30pm Livestream on Zoom

AND

FRIDAY | OCT 23 | 1:00-6:30pm In-person at Yoga Sanctuary

Cost $179 | HYTT grads $129

Would you like to learn how to create inclusive spaces for students who have experienced trauma?

This training will provide a solid foundation of understanding for you to create and teach yoga classes that help students heal, integrate, and come back into the body. Topics of study include:

-Neurobiology of Trauma - Explore how trauma affects the physical body and the nervous system including polyvagal theory.

-Creating a Safe Space - Learn how to use clear, empowering language and sequencing to foster a sense of choice, security and agency.

-Awareness of Racial and Generational Trauma - Understand how systemic oppression can manifest in the body.

-Ethical Considerations - Understand the scope of a yoga teacher's role and when it's appropriate to refer students to mental health professionals.

-Embodied Practices - Explore specific techniques, such as grounding and breathwork, that can help students reconnect with their bodies at their own pace.

After study and discussion, we will also dig in with a teaching lab. This enables each person to practice how to teach these elements with mentored support and constructive feedback. The heart of Trauma-Informed teachings is about sharing power and stepping into your own agency - so this isn’t a dogmatic list of “do or don’t”. Discussion will be encouraged as each person experiments with which elements of the Trauma-Informed model best suits their teaching style.

This training of “Teaching Yoga Through a Trauma-Informed Lens” is eligible for 8 hours of Yoga Alliance Continuing Education for yoga teachers. Live attendance at all meetings is necessary to receive a CEU certificate.

long_description:
Move & breathe with P4L + Cuties Los Angeles!

About this Event

Unwind through gentle movement and honest reflection in this P4L and collaboration that pairs a grounding yin yoga practice with guided journaling. We'll flow through the body first, then settle into stillness with the page - creating space to process, release, and reconnect with self. All levels and bodies welcome; no writing or yoga experience required. Mats will be provided.

Tickets
Parenting for Liberation believes that Black parents and families deserve access to creative and healing spaces without the barrier of cost. We believe in reducing and eliminating barriers to our program offerings when possible, and we also believe in equity and resource sharing. Tickets to our 10 year programming allows us to continue serving our community in the long-term. Please see the descriptions below to determine which ticket level is best for you.
Complimentary tickets - Supports our community members that want to attend but simply don’t have the means at the moment. We encourage folks to sign up early since there are a limited amount available for the event.

Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

Light Up the Night at Navratri 2026 - Live Garba and Dandiya Night by Pancham Beats
Mark your calendars for the 15th of October, 2026, as Pancham Beats LLC brings you an unforgettable night of celebration and dance at the Navratri 2026 - Live Garba and Dandiya Night. Experience the joy of Navratri, one of the most vibrant festivals celebrated with great fervor and enthusiasm. Lose yourself in the rhythmic beats of Garba and Dandiya, traditional dance forms from the Indian state of Gujarat. This event is a perfect blend of Bollywood, Dance, and Religious festivities that caters to all Hindi and Gujarati speaking audience. So, dress in your vibrant ethnic best and join us in celebrating Navratri in a grand style.
Meet the Maestro - Dhawal Majmudar
At the heart of this musical extravaganza is the versatile artist, Dhawal Majmudar. With over a decade of experience in performing across the San Francisco Bay Area, Dhawal is a force to reckon with in the music industry. His musical mastery includes a wide range of genres from Garba, Dandiya, Indian Folk, Bollywood, Bhajans to Ghazals. Known for his entertaining voice impressions, most notably of the legendary Amitabh Bachchan, Dhawal's performances are always filled with energy and charisma. A man of many talents, Dhawal is ready to mesmerize you with his music at the Navratri 2026 - Live Garba and Dandiya Night.
Experience the Vibrancy at Shubham Halls
The Navratri 2026 - Live Garba and Dandiya Night will be held at the Shubham Halls, located at 1214 Apollo Way, Sunnyvale, CA, United States. Known for its safety and accessibility, Shubham Halls is an ideal venue for large gatherings and celebrations. Around the venue, you can enjoy a variety of Indian restaurants, perfect for those looking to indulge in some authentic Indian cuisine before or after the event. A gentle, grounding yoga practice influenced by Yin & Restorative Yoga, designed to slow down, release tension, and reconnect.

About this Event

Chill Yoga with Jason is a gentle, grounding practice designed to help you slow down, reconnect, and settle into the present moment.
Heavily influenced by Yin and Restorative Yoga, Jason will guide a steady, unhurried flow incorporating longer-held shapes, intentional stillness, and supported postures to encourage release, relaxation, and deeper awareness of the body.
The practice is spacious and grounding, with an emphasis on mindful pacing, intentional movement, and creating a sense of calm both on and off the mat. Options and modifications will be offered throughout, making the class welcoming for both newer students and experienced yogis alike.
This is a donation-based class, with a portion of proceeds benefiting the NW Community Food Bank and Van Ness Main Street, helping support the organizations and community that make these gatherings possible.
Please bring your own mat. Some props will be provided, though you are welcome to bring any additional props you prefer, such as blocks, straps, or blankets.
As part of Yoga on Connecticut, our community yoga project, we're excited to continue creating opportunities for neighbors to gather through movement, mindfulness, and meaningful connection.
Plan to arrive a few minutes early to settle in and set up your space before class begins.

long_description:
Join Tamika Caston-Miller this fall at Brick City Yoga! 

Yoga for Larger Bodies is a 3-hour, hands-on workshop designed to challenge outdated narratives and make space for real, lived experiences in the room. We’ll explore practical principles, break down common pose struggles, and workshop accessible variations that actually work for larger bodies—no forcing, no shrinking, no pretending.

This space is for anyone who’s ever felt like they had to “figure it out” on their own in a yoga class, as well as teachers who want to show up with more awareness, skill, and respect when guiding bodies of all sizes. Expect real talk, supportive exploration, and a whole lot of permission to move in ways that make sense for your body.

long_description:
Therapeutic Hot Yoga goes through the traditional 26 Hatha

yoga postures, beginning and ending with a breathing exercise. This

class is accessible for anyone regardless of age or ability level. It is an

ideal place to start your practice if you are new or a beginner. You will

feel the therapeutic benefits after just one session. The room is heated

from 90 degrees which helps your muscles warm up for deeper

stretching and promotes detoxification through sweat. There are no sun

salutations so it easy on the wrists and shoulders. The first portion of the

class is done standing where we focus on creating strength, stamina,

and balance. The second half is on the floor where the focus shifts

heavily to spinal mobility. You will be guided through every posture step

by step. Each instruction is given so that your body works optimally and

safely. Every class is the same but your experience, awareness and

perception changes each time you practice. Through consistency in a

structured program you will be able to deepen your internal experience

and track your progress. 26&2 classes are simple, consistent and

effective.

Mark your calendars for the electrifying evening of October 15th, 2026. Pancham Beats invites you to immerse yourself in a night filled with live music, pulsating beats, and invincible energy at our Bay Area Garba, Raas & Dandia Night. A must-attend for all Gujarati and Multilingual music enthusiasts, this event promises an unforgettable celebration of Navratri/Dandiya traditions set to the rhythm of our vibrant, multicultural community.
Meet the Maestro: Dhawal Majmudar
Behind the captivating melodies and heart-thumping beats of Pancham Beats is the seasoned vocalist and musician, Dhawal Majmudar. With a career spanning over a decade, Dhawal has established a reputation as one of the most versatile and entertaining performers in the Bay Area. His performances, marked by a rich blend of Indian musical traditions and contemporary sounds, have endeared him to audiences of all ages. Whether it's Garba, Dandiya, Bhajans, Indian Folk, Bollywood, or Ghazals, Dhawal's mastery over diverse genres is truly impressive. Moreover, his unique talent for voice impressions, notably his remarkable rendition of Amitabh Bachchan, adds a delightful twist to his performances, making him a crowd favourite at every event.

SHUBHAM HALLS, located at 1214 Apollo Way in Sunnyvale, CA, United States, is the chosen venue for this grand celebration. long_description:
Fall Yoga Retreat: A Refuge for Your Heart

October 16-18, 2026

with Chaya Spencer at Lifebridge Sanctuary, Rosendale, NY

A true refuge is more than a place. It is a space where the mind grows quiet, the body softens, and the heart feels safe. It is where we can set down the weight of daily responsibilities, reconnect with what matters most, and remember the steady center that lives within us. In times of challenge, refuge restores us. In times of ease, it deepens our connection to ourselves and to one another.

Join us for a nourishing weekend retreat at Lifebridge Sanctuary, nestled in the beauty of the Catskills. Through yoga, meditation, time in nature, wholesome meals, meaningful conversation, and spacious periods of rest and reflection, you’ll be invited to slow down and settle into a deeper sense of presence and belonging.

In the yogic tradition, there is a beautiful Sanskrit phrase: hridaya vishranti—reposing in the heart. Here, “heart” does not refer to the physical organ or even the emotional heart, but to our essential nature, the innermost core of who we are. Vishranti means rest, repose, or deep relaxation. Together, these words point to the experience of resting in our own being, returning home to ourselves.

This retreat offers a supportive cocoon for renewal and self-discovery. Come away for a weekend of rest, connection, and renewal. Return home grounded, refreshed, and reconnected to the essence of who you are.

Our retreat center, Lifebridge Sanctuary, offers us a space of peace, nature and quiet to introspect, practice yoga, eat well and rest in beauty inside and out. The Sanctuary is a 12,000 square foot hand crafted, green facility on 95 acres of forest and spectacular open space on the Northern crest of the Shawangunk Ridge, less than 90 minutes from Shree.

title: REZN
venue_name: 7 S Broadway, Denver, CO, United States, Colorado 80209
description: REZN
long_description:
REZN – the Chicago-based band of Rob McWilliams (vocals, guitar), Phil Cangelosi (bass), Patrick Dunn (drums), and Spencer Ouellette (synth/saxophone) – announce their new album, Burden, out June 14th via their new label Sargent House. In conjunction, they present its massive lead single/video, “Chasm.” Since their inception, REZN have mined the stark monochromatic depths of underground metal and fused them with the kaleidoscopic delights of psychedelia, prog rock, and shoegaze. With their latest album Burden, they plumb the deepest, bleakest trenches of their sound while retaining a lifeline into the cosmos. Staking a claim at the crossroads of the hazy dimensions of modern psych acts like Black Angels, the cavernous gloom and reverb-drenched guitar of bands like Spectral Voice, and the lurching low-end meditations of artists like OM, REZN have created Burden—an album of immense amp-worshipping weight and intoxicating instrumentation.

Burden was recorded simultaneously with their previous album Solace back in July 2021 at Earth Analog Studios in Tolono, IL by Matt Russell. Rather than release a double album, REZN divided the material into two separate records, each with its own distinct emotional timbre. Whereas Solace was meant to uplift and create a sense of narcotic dreaminess, Burden skews towards the themes of delirium, claustrophobia, and misery. Musically, Burden favors riffs over atmosphere, percussion over ether, dissonance over beauty, but there is still an undeniable cohesion between it and its predecessor. The marriage of brute force and sublime textures has always been a key tactic in REZN’s approach—a duality that may explain their touring history with fellow synesthesia-inducing metallurgists Elder and Russian Circles—but the spectrum of the band’s mercurial temperaments has never felt as clearly defined and fully explored as it does on Burden.

long_description:
What: The Art of Sequencing: A workshop for Yoga Teachers

When: Friday, October 16th | 6pm-9pm

Where: Megan’s Yoga Tribe Downtown Lee’s Summit 10 SW 3rd Street Lee’s Summit, MO 64063 (Front Studio)

Investment in Teaching: $50

This workshop is for Yoga Instructors

Every yoga class tells a story through movement.

It begins somewhere, builds toward something, and eventually asks us to slow down, integrate, and rest. The art of sequencing is learning how to create that journey with thoughtfulness and intention.

In this 3-hour Yoga Krama workshop, we'll take a closer look at what happens between the first breath and final savasana. We'll explore progression, transitions, pacing, class timing, and the many choices that shape the experience of a yoga practice.

We'll consider how to:

Create progression that feels natural and purposeful

Prepare the body for more complex or challenging movements

Use transitions to connect rather than simply move between poses

Work within the practical framework of a 45-, 60-, or 75-minute class

Balance movement and stillness, effort and recovery

Make thoughtful choices based on the students in front of you

Then we'll take it off the page and onto the mat.

In small groups, you'll work together to develop sequences, consider timing and progression, and explore how your choices affect the experience of the practice. We'll have time to move through our ideas, make adjustments, and learn from one another.

This is an opportunity to step back from the individual pose and look at the bigger picture of the practice.

Where are we starting? Where are we going? And how do we create a journey that makes sense along the way?

Meet Your Teacher Grace Ames:

With over two decades of experience on the mat, Grace brings both depth and lightness to her teaching. Trained at Teach to Inspire Yoga Education Center, she has been guiding students since 2005. Her style is challenging yet playful, encouraging curiosity in every posture. By emphasizin

long_description:
Functional Yin Yoga + the Subtle Body is a training for anyone looking to spend more time with their practice and understand it in a deeper, more thoughtful way.

We’ll explore Yin through a functional lens—looking at how anatomy, shape, and individual differences influence the way poses feel in the body. Alongside that, we’ll bring in the Subtle Body to build awareness that goes beyond the physical and supports a more grounded, connected practice.

This 20-hour training is a good fit for both teachers and dedicated students, especially those interested in practicing and sharing yoga in ways that are more inclusive and responsive. Whether this is your first Yin training or you’ve studied it before, you’ll walk away with a clearer foundation and tools you can actually use.

Yoga Alliance teachers can receive 20 hours of Continuing Education credits.

title: Trauma Informed Yoga Teacher Training
venue_name: Pilgrimage of the Heart Yoga - Normal Heights
description: Trauma informed yoga aims to create a welcoming space for anyone who is experiencing the difficulties that can result from traumatic events.
long_description:
Trauma informed yoga aims to create a welcoming space for anyone who is experiencing the difficulties that can result from traumatic events.

About this Event

Trauma is an emotional response to a stressful or disturbing incident or physical injury. When one experiences a traumatic event, it can create an inner environment that will affect many aspects of the survivor’s life. From a sense of disconnection to a dysregulated nervous system, the impact of trauma reaches both the mind and the body and can leave one with feelings of insecurity, overwhelm and powerlessness that can distance the survivor from their innate sense of joy and inner peace.
Yoga has many tools that can reconnect practitioners to their inner peace and well-being, but for those living with the inner wound of trauma, a regular yoga class may present challenges that keep them from enjoying the many benefits of the practice.
Trauma informed yoga aims to create a welcoming space for anyone who is experiencing the difficulties that can result from traumatic events.
Join Lauren McLaren to investigate the impact of trauma and explore how to make your classes inclusive and sensitive to the needs of those who are living with the effects of trauma.
During this 14-hour training, you will learn:
How trauma can affect physical health and well-beingThe neurobiology of trauma and how yoga can assist in regulating the nervous system to help reconnect the body/mind systemsHow to use practices including asana, pranayama, mudra and mindfulness to promote empowerment and agencyHow to honor trauma survivors in yoga classes by tailoring language and cues, providing consistency in structure, and offering modificationsThis training is perfect for teachers who want to create a more inclusive teaching environment as well as for practitioners who are looking to advance their knowledge in how yogic tools can serve this population.
Please note that this training is not intended to empower teachers to diagnose or treat trauma

title: Rewiring Time: How Yoga Works on the Past, Present & Future
description: Hosted by Brenna Geehan, Oct 17 - 1PM at Haight Studio
long_description:
Hosted by Brenna Geehan, Oct 17 - 1PM at Haight Studio

About this Event

Why does yoga actually work?

Not why it feels good. Why a consistent practice changes how you move through your life.

This 2.5 hour workshop explores an idea: asana works on your past, pranayama works on your present, meditation works on your future. We'll practice all three separately, so you can feel the difference in your own body.

In asana, you'll notice what your body has been quietly holding onto. In pranayama, you'll discover what it feels like to be fully here, breath by breath. In meditation, you'll practice meeting what's ahead with more steadiness than you brought in the door.

You'll leave with a much clearer sense of why a complete practice, not a workout, is what creates lasting change. And a sense of how much further this goes.

No experience with breathwork or meditation required. Just curiosity.

description: Join us for a unique outdoor yoga experience that combines beginner friendly yoga, fresh air, laughter, and plenty of goat interaction. long_description:
Join us for a unique outdoor yoga experience that combines beginner friendly yoga, fresh air, laughter, and plenty of goat interaction. Whether you’re coming with friends, family, coworkers, or just looking for a fun and memorable outing, goat yoga is designed to be relaxed and enjoyable for all experience levels.

Please dress appropriately for the weather, as this is an outdoor event.

For safety reasons, children under the age of 5 are not permitted inside the fenced goat yoga participation area at any time, including as observers or accompanying guests.

Know Before You Go:

• Please do not enter the fenced goat yoga area earlier than 15 minutes before your scheduled class time. We’ll leave extra time after class for photos and socializing with the goats.

• BYOM (Bring Your Own Mat) — We do not provide yoga mats, but large towels will be available for all attendees. We also provide bottled water, sunscreen, bug spray, hand sanitizer, and wipes.

• Be prepared for our goats to take an interest in you! Goat yoga is designed to be lighthearted and interactive. Our goats may nudge, nibble, scratch, jump, or step on guests during class. Children ages 5+ are welcome with a participating parent or guardian.

• Most of our goats are Nigerian Dwarf goats and are generally under 25 pounds, though some of our larger personalities can occasionally reach 30–35 pounds.

• Our goats are not potty trained animals. While we do our best to keep the space clean throughout the session, occasional droppings are a normal and expected part of the experience. Sanitizing stations and antibacterial wipes will be available.

• All attendees must check in and complete a provided liability waiver prior to class. Masks are not required. Social distancing and personal comfort levels regarding proximity to others are left to each attendee’s discretion.

Our tribe looks forward to meeting you!

About this Event

Soul in the Sequence
The Art of Creating Meaningful Yoga Experiences

What makes a yoga class more than a collection of poses?
Soul in the Sequence is a 3-hour continuing education training designed for yoga teachers who want to deepen their understanding of sequencing while exploring how intention, storytelling, creativity, and clear cueing can transform the student experience.
Join two experienced E-RYT-500 yoga teachers, each bringing a unique perspective and years of teaching experience to the room. Together, we’ll explore both the foundations of thoughtful sequencing and the creative possibilities that emerge when we begin to see a yoga class as an experience with an arc, rhythm, and purpose.
This training will include:
Traditional sequencing principles and methodologyCreative and intentional sequencingBuilding an effective class arcStorytelling through movementUsing music and musicality with intentionClear, effective cueingOpportunities to practice teaching and receive feedbackSpace to explore and develop your own teaching voiceThis is an interactive training, not simply a lecture. You’ll have the opportunity to learn, observe, create, teach, and receive feedback alongside other yoga teachers.
Whether you’re newer to teaching or have been teaching for years, Soul in the Sequence is an opportunity to revisit the foundations, explore new possibilities, and consider how your own perspective and creativity can shape the classes you offer.

Wellbeing Weekends is a six-week beginner-friendly programme for the residents of the Coalfields. Finish off your week of hard work with relaxation in nature. 

To gain the most from our programme, we recommend you come to all six sessions, but if you cannot make it to all the sessions, just message Lyze to let them know.

Sessions, which should be booked separately, include:

Texture Printing – We will explore Elemore park using our senses to help relax our minds and body. We will spend time focused on the physical space that we inhabit and make prints of the interesting textures that we come across. 

Wild Yoga for all with Roy Moor – We will be joined by Wild Yoga instructor Roy Moor for a session of relaxation for our minds and bodies. Wild Yoga is suitable for all abilities and will take place amongst the swaying trees and bird song at Elemore park. 

Seasons changing Wildlife Walk – Join us for a gentle walk around Elemore park to observe how nature reacts to the changing of seasons. Learn how to identify native trees, birds and mushrooms thriving in the Autumnal weather. 

Spooky Sunderland – Tell spooky stories about the myths and legends of Sunderland and make ghosts, witches, and creepy crawlies from natural and recycled materials. 

Art within Nature – Inspired by Andy Goldsworthy, make temporary art using sticks, rocks and leaves in collaboration with nature.  

Bug hotel crafts – Help out bugs in your garden or local green space by making a bug hotel for them to make their home over the colder months. We will use recycled and foraged materials to create hanging hotels and discover what might come to stay. 

Please ensure that, if they are attending the programme with you, places are booked for any carers or support workers as this will help us to organise our equipment and keep our register accurate.

long_description:
$55 ENROLL: https://www.yogashalasac.com/events/free-your-neck-shoulders-wm93g

“Hips hold many stories” — Gabrielle Roth

Love my once a quarter time with you at Shala. This time HIPS. We all need this one because...

Hips hold us—physically, emotionally, energetically. This immersive workshop deepens your understanding of one of the body’s most important—and often misunderstood—areas. Feel your way inside this territory through the integrated lens of yoga and physical therapy. Deepen your understanding of hip anatomy, mobility and stability. Feel how common patterns of tension and compensation impact posture and alignment.

This practice invites curiosity over force, connection over performance and presence over perfection. Open to all levels, including yoga practitioners, movement professionals and anyone curious about creating a healthier relationship with their body.

Roller density is so important. If you have one that hurts, come try something else! Rollers and balls available for trial and/or purchase. If you have your own, please bring. 

Bio:

Bella Dreizler is a physical therapist and guide of yoga & 5Rhythms. She brings body wisdom infused with heart and soul to dance floor, yoga mat and treatment table. More information: www.bodyjoy.net

Dr. Shelley Best (RYT-200) is a yoga teacher, mindfulness meditation teacher, sound practitioner, and creator of The Phoenix Practice™. Her path began at West Hartford Yoga, where - only a few classes in - a middle-of-the-night calling sent her to India within two and a half weeks. At the ashram of Sri Mata Amritanandamayi - Amma, "the hugging saint" - in Kerala, she immersed in Amrita Yoga and the Integrated Amrita Meditation technique under Amma's personal guidance. India is where her own healing began.

She carried that healing home.

Alongside Barbara Ruzansky, founder of West Hartford Yoga, she co-founded a community yoga studio inside Hartford's 224 EcoSpace - making the practice reachable for everyone, including those who might never otherwise walk through a studio door.

title: Ayurveda for Fall: Yoga, Nourishment + Seasonal Self-Care
description: Fall Ayurveda + yoga to calm your nervous system, nourish your body and discover seasonal practices to help you feel more balanced.
long_description:
Fall Ayurveda + yoga to calm your nervous system, nourish your body and discover seasonal practices to help you feel more balanced.

About this Event

As the days grow shorter and the air turns crisp, we often feel an inner shift. In Ayurveda, fall is known as Vata season - a time defined by the energy of wind, movement, and change.
When this energy rises in the natural world, it can show up within us as an unsettled mind, restless sleep, joint discomfort, dry skin, or irregular digestion.
This seasonal shift is also an invitation to slow down, nourish yourself, and create more stability. Ayurveda offers time-honored practices to help support the body and nervous system as we move from summer into fall.
Join Michele for a seasonal Ayurveda and yoga workshop designed to help you move through fall feeling grounded, replenished, and warmed from the inside out.

WHAT WE’LL EXPLORE:Movement:
A slow, centering yoga practice for fall with an emphasis on calming the nervous system, releasing tension from the hips and spine, and using the breath as a steady anchor.
Nourishment:
Ayurvedic principles for maintaining vitality through warming seasonal foods, soothing self-care rituals, and daily habits that support greater stability as the season deepens.

WHAT YOU’LL LEAVE WITH:A short home yoga practice and approachable Ayurvedic self-care rituals you can return to throughout the fall season.
When the world outside feels blustery and unpredictable, you’ll have practices to help you reconnect with what feels steady within, leaving you feeling nourished, centered, and with a deeper understanding of what brings you back into balance.
No previous experience with Ayurveda or yoga is necessary.

long_description:
Come together with kindred spirits at RAINBOW RESONANCE — a *DONATION-BASED* community *SOUND BATH* created by and for *QUEER + TRANS* folks. This "sonic journey for QTies" offers an intentional and accessible monthly space to soften, breathe, and just be. 

Whether you're arriving joyful, exhausted, overwhelmed, or simply curious, you're invited to settle in, release tension, and let melodic sound support your nervous system. Crystal bowls, harp, and soft guidance create space for relaxation, grounding, and emotional reset.

ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR: Charlie Sebastian Short is a certified sound practitioner, musician, and caregiver based in Portland. His work draws from the Quantum Sound Method, classical music training, and years of supporting both humans and animals with patience and care. He approaches sound healing as nervous system support, using harmonious instruments to encourage rest, calm, and emotional ease. As a mixed-race, LGBTQIA+, and neurodivergent practitioner, Charlie creates an inclusive space where all bodies and identities can access comfort and relaxation.

"There is something profoundly different about resting in a space created by people who understand. I created Rainbow Resonance at @lighthousecommunityyogapdx for my LGBTQIA+ community because many of us know what it feels like to move through the world carrying chronic stress, hypervigilance, and the weight of simply existing. We deserve spaces where our nervous systems can soften without explanation. 

Each sound bath is unique. Every gathering responds to the energy of the room and the people in it, so each experience unfolds a little differently and supports whatever you may be carrying in that moment. 

Healing doesn't only happen in solitude. There is something powerful about breathing, resting, and sharing space with other queer and trans people, whether you arrive with friends or meet someone new. Community itself can be restorative.

title: Sunday Somatics - Healing with Yoga: Session 1
description: A beginner-friendly yoga series taught by Rhya Moffitt. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.
long_description:
A beginner-friendly yoga series taught by Rhya Moffitt. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.

About this Event

This beginner-friendly yoga series features a heart-centered, healing slow flow practice intimately linked to the Smart's How Do We Heal? 2026-2027 exhibition. Held in the museum lobby, the series features gentle movements and contemplative prompts that begin by exploring the various sources of suffering from which we might seek to heal—the physical, emotional, structural, ancestral—then move to methods and practices for healing. This 75-minute class culminates with aromatherapy, breathwork, and contemplative viewing of intentionally selected pieces from the How Do We Heal? collection. Class is led by certified yoga instructor Rhya Moffitt who guides practice with the intention of cultivating inner stillness, awareness, and presence. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.

The first four sessions move through various sources of suffering:
1. physical (health & illness),
2. emotional (loss, grief, and renewal),
3. structural / collective (displacement), and
4. ancestral (trauma)

The last two sessions get into the how with a focus on:
5. wholeness, integration, (mind, body, and spirit) and
6. supportive healing modalities (healing objects).

Free; RSVP encouraged. Limited number of mats available.

Photo by Mateusz Patrzyk.

long_description:
45 minutes of outdoor puppy yoga in Stoney's Good Time Ranch, followed by an open puppy cuddle hour. Net proceeds go to a local rescue.

About this Event

Puppy yoga, East Austin style — in a backyard built for it.

Join Kitten Paws and Downward Dogs at Stoney's Good Time Ranch for 45 minutes of gentle, all-levels yoga in their fully fenced, shaded backyard, with adoptable rescue puppies loose among the mats. Fans and misters running, coffee and matcha pop-up open, and no one minding if a puppy interrupts your flow.

Then the puppies stay. When class ends, the yard opens for a full hour of puppy cuddles and photos — no ticket needed for that part. Bring a friend who'd rather skip the yoga, grab a coffee, and hang out with the pups. Donations to the rescue are gladly accepted.

The puppies are the point. Every puppy is a rescue and is looking for a home. Our rescue partner brings the puppies, their pen and their volunteers, so you can meet, cuddle and start an adoption conversation on the spot.

Where the money goes. Proceeds from this event go to a local Austin rescue. We will announce our rescue partner here as soon as they are confirmed, and the event is held in their honour with the net proceeds going straight to them.

Discover the voice of your soul in this transformative workshop with internationally touring world music artist, teacher, and author Girish.

About this Event

A deep dive into transformational Breathwork, healing Mantra, and revitalizing Chi Gong with beloved yogi-musician & author, GIRISH. The PRANA RISING IMMERSION invites us to experience a radically expanded sense of our potential, our vitality, our wellness and wisdom through the transformational power of these ancient practices:
THE BREATH OF LIFE (9 HEALING BREATHS)
WIM HOF METHOD
PRIMAL CHI GONG
THE FIVE TIBETANS
MANTRA & CHANTING
The PRANA RISING IMMERSION workshop offers us the opportunity to experience a radically expanded sense of our potential, our vitality, our wellness and wisdom.
About the artist
Girish is an internationally touring world music artist, teacher, and author. He began his music career as a jazz drummer, spent five years as a monk in a Hindu monastery, returned to music as a session tabla player on more than a hundred world music albums, and for the past twelve years has written, recorded, and performed his own original music and taught Sanskrit mantras and chanting in music festivals and yoga studios all over the world. His seven albums have received critical acclaim from O, The Oprah Magazine, Yoga Journal, and The Guardian, among others. Girish's book, Music and Mantras, continues Girish's mission to share the art of meditation through music and mantra with the world.
This in-person-only event is sponsored by Hartford International University's Center for Transformative Spirituality.

The fourth full-length from Basement, Beside Myself is an intimate look at the drawbacks of living in your own head, and the attempt to shake off everyday anxieties. “One of the things everyone in the band seems to struggle with is living fully in the present time,” says Andrew Fisher, who co-founded the Ipswich, England-bred five-piece in 2010. “We tend to look back on the past and think, ‘That was so much better than what’s going on now,’ or look toward the future and assume it’s going to be better than today. The title came from thinking about, ‘Wouldn’t it be great if you could stop yourself from doing that, and just appreciate the moment as it happens?’” 

But for all its intense introspection and confessions of self-consciousness, Beside Myself centers on a powerful, passionately charged sound that makes every track feel deeply cathartic. A relentless burst of pure vitality, the album expresses its unrest in the language of furious guitar riffs and visceral rhythms. And at the heart of Beside Myself are Basement’s indelible melodies, an element that lends an anthemic quality to even the most heavy-hearted songs. 

The follow-up to Promise Everything—a 2016 album whose re-release the following year marked Basement’s debut for Fueled by Ramen—Beside Myself was co-produced by the band and Colin Brittain, and mixed by Rich Costey (Arctic Monkeys, Foo Fighters, Muse). description: A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.
long_description:
A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.

About this Event

Cleveland Rape Crisis Center invites survivors of rape and sexual abuse to a free community yoga class. This class is designed to be a safe space for survivors to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. This practice will allow students an opportunity to increase body awareness in support of greater physical, emotional and mental well being.
We will explore breathing practices and therapeutic movement to help survivors in connecting mindfully to the moment. We will learn ways to listen to our bodies and breath so we can honor our own unique experience and needs.

Who can attend?
Survivors of sexual violence/sexual trauma.All yoga experience levels welcome.All genders welcome.Survivors ages 13-17 may attend if accompanied by a parent/guardian. Please register the adult and child separately.

About Dana:
Dana has been practicing and teaching yoga for 20 years. She has trained in a variety of modalities and has learned from many amazing teachers over the years. Her most recent work has been focused on teaching yoga + mindfulness to kids ages K-8, as well as providing Trauma Informed Yoga classes for the community.
“I am deeply committed to this path and am grateful for the opportunity to share all the beautiful healing benefits these practices can provide. Along with my work in schools and as a trauma informed yoga teacher, I am also a mother and musician. I am passionate about creating communities that can support and uplift us all.”

About this Event

Sound Bath + Yoga Nidra San Diego
Experience a deeply restorative Sound Bath + Yoga Nidra San Diego designed to help you unwind, reset your nervous system, and reconnect with yourself in a calm, supportive space.
This immersive session blends the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls with the guided meditation of Yoga Nidra, creating a powerful experience for stress relief, emotional balance, and deep rest.

✨ What is Yoga Nidra?Yoga Nidra, also known as “yogic sleep,” is a guided meditation practice that brings you into a state between wakefulness and sleep. While your body fully relaxes, your mind remains gently aware.
During Yoga Nidra, you’ll be guided through breath awareness, body scanning, and visualization techniques that help:
• Calm the nervous system
• Reduce stress and anxiety
• Improve sleep quality
• Support emotional healing and clarity
It’s often said that one hour of Yoga Nidra can feel like several hours of sleep, making it one of the most effective practices for deep restoration.

🎶 What to ExpectYou’ll be comfortably supported as you lie down and are guided through Yoga Nidra, followed by a soothing sound bath using crystal singing bowls and other instruments. The vibrations help quiet the mind and bring your body into a deeply relaxed, meditative state.
No prior meditation or sound bath experience is necessary. Simply arrive, get comfortable, and receive.

title: Pépin Lecture Series - Safar with Madhushree Ghosh
description: Join Madhushree Ghosh as she discusses her book, Safar: Finding Home, History, and Culture through Punjabi Food in the American West!
long_description:
Join Madhushree Ghosh as she discusses her book, Safar: Finding Home, History, and Culture through Punjabi Food in the American West!

About this Event

This event will be live steamed on Zoom. You can select an in-person or virtual ticket. Virtual ticket holders will receive a Zoom link prior to the event.

Madhushree Ghosh (Phd in biochemistry) is the author of Khabaar: An Immigrant Journey of Food, Memory and Family and SAFAR: Finding Home, History, and Culture through Punjabi Food in the American West. She is the creative founder of KhabaarCo, a global literary salon and supper club. As a TEDx Speaker, Madhushree interrogates cultural, culinary and immigration issues using food as a social justice tool.

Published in June of this year, Safar blends memoir and history to explore the role of Punjabi food in fostering community and identity among South Asian refugees and immigrants.

Safar follows the journey of South Asian refugees, immigrants, and their children-in particular, Sikhs, Jats, and Muslims-who moved to the southwestern states of America over centuries as farmers, truck drivers, restaurant owners, and dhaba/diner stall cooks. An expedition in search of the asli-or real Punjabi food-Madhushree Ghosh explores how their food traveled from pre-partition British India to now, while weaving in her own immigrant journey as a graduate student to America in 1993, her quest to find home through the food of her Bengali refugee parents, and the physical journey she embarked on to visit the Punjabi communities in California, Arizona, and New Mexico.

Focusing on four Punjabi women, each a part of a different immigration wave of South Asia to the American West, Ghosh highlights the food and recipes they brought with them that connect them to their pasts. Safar shares stories of displacement, discrimination, community, and hope, while shedding light on immigrant journeys and the true meaning of home, comfort food, and what constitutes a “true Punjabi” meal. long_description:
With Kehlani's music as a guide, we'll experience a gentle beginner's yoga flow led by certified yogi and award-winning author Arriel Vinson.

We’ll begin with a gentle warm up before moving into a sequence that will allow us to let go of the day. At the end of our flow, we’ll experience a guided meditation—one that reminds us to be confident, speak life into ourselves, and release all that isn’t serving us.

Please arrive 15-20 minutes early to allow time for parking and checking in. If you have a mat, please bring one as mats are limited!

**About the facilitator:**

Arriel Vinson started taking her yoga practice seriously in 2021 to counteract her stressful work life. What she discovered was a clearer mind, a desire to deepen her practice, and a calling to make more space for Black practitioners. As a CYT-200, certified by Cityoga in Indianapolis, Arriel hopes to show students that yoga is more than a fitness practice: meditation, breathwork, and asanas create a path toward understanding ourselves, and the world, better. They’re tools for liberation, resistance, and community building. An author by profession, Arriel incorporates journaling and affirmations into her classes to emphasize the constant need for loving ourselves and finding compassion in a society that often encourages the opposite. title: Beyond Thinking: A Holosomatic Breathwork Experience
description:
Small by design. Deep by intention.
Somatic Group Breathwork Class - 14 participants max
long_description:
Small by design. Deep by intention.

Somatic Group Breathwork Class - 14 participants max

About this Event

A monthly Holosomatic Breathwork in Denver, Colorado
What if you stopped trying to think your way through it and started listening to what your body already knows?
We spend so much of our lives in our heads: thinking, analyzing, overthinking, pushing through and trying to figure out what to do next.
But sometimes, understanding something isn't enough to create change.
Holosomatic Breathwork is an immersive, body-based breathwork experience designed to take you beyond thinking and into the felt experience of your body.
Through intentional breathing, body awareness, music and guided somatic practice, you'll be invited to slow down, turn inward, and explore what may be ready to shift—without needing to force, fix, or figure it all out.

What you might experienceEvery breathwork session is different, and there is nothing you need to achieve or perform.
You may find space to:
Reconnect with your body and your inner experienceBecome more aware of sensations, emotions, and patterns beneath the surfaceRelease tension or emotions you've been carryingExplore a deeper sense of presence and connectionPractice nervous system awareness and regulationMove beyond habitual thinking and into embodied experienceDiscover what becomes possible when you create space to simply feelThis is a small, intimate group experience with a maximum of 14 participants, intentionally designed to feel personal, supportive and grounded.
You don't need to know how to meditate.
You don't need previous breathwork experience.
You don't need to be "good" at breathwork.
And you definitely don't need to have everything figured out.
Just come as you are.
Wildly Regulated is rooted in the belief that your body holds its own innate wisdom.
When we begin to listen—to sensation, breath, emotion, and the signals of the nervous system—we can begin to develop a different relationship with ourselves.

Description:Yoga to Regulate is a continuing progression of the Yoga techniques introduced in the Osher Center's M1 yoga classes. This M2 series specifically focuses on increasing mobility and stability, especially in the spine and trunk. Standing, seated, and lying positions will be offered, as well as specific breathing practices and meditation. Individual modifications are always available. This M2 series is suitable for those with some experience in practicing Yoga and for those comfortable moving on their own.

Vinyasa means to link breath with movement in a special way to achieve a particular outcome. You will learn to let the breath guide your movement as the ultimate teacher. The second half of class (Yin) will focus on deep stretches with long holds (1-5 min). You will be invited to relax and release any muscular contraction, working deep into the connective tissue. Mark your calendars for 23rd October 2026, as the Gujarati Cultural Association of Bay Area, or GCA, brings you an evening of vibrant traditional Gujarati festivities at the GCA Bay Area Ras Garba event. Organized by the Aanal & Achal Anjaria Team and Sharda Musical Group, this event is set to immerse you in the heart of Gujarat's rich culture. Their profound understanding of traditional music and their ability to infuse it with contemporary elements has made them a favorite among audiences worldwide. Their performance is sure to resonate with each attendee, leaving a lasting impression of the vibrant Gujarati culture.
Experience the Event at the Historic Washington High School

title: Goat Yoga in The Patch @ Bedford Public Library!
description: Goat Yoga in The Patch @ Bedford Public Library!
long_description:
Come and join us for Goat Yoga in The Patch hosted by the Bedford Public Library!

About this Event 
 https://cdn-az.allevents.in/events2/banners/dcb6ced0-87e3-11f1-b6c8-ef4137d8dcb0-rimg-w663-h740-dca7c3f1-gmir.jpg 

YOU are invited to GOAT YOGA in BEDFORD, TX! Come and get your yoga on while our tribe of pet goats graze and jump around (or on) you! We will be in the pumpkin patch at the Bedford Public Library! Come as you are or dressed up in Halloween costume attire. The goats will be in costume!
Please come dressed for the weather as the event will be outside. Proceeds from this class directly benefit our animals and our local non-profit initiatives. 

Know before you go:
*Please do not enter the fenced off goat yoga area any earlier than 15 minutes before your scheduled class time. We will set aside time after class for extra socializing and picture taking with the goats if you don't get the shot you want during yoga practice.
 *BYOM (bring your own yoga mat) We do not provide mats, but we do provide beach towels for all attendees to use. We also provide bottled waters, sunscreen, bug spray, etc.
*Be prepared for our goats to take an interest in you! They are excited to be with you! SUSANNA CAGLE: WWW.ATTUNE.YOGA [ http://www.attune.yoga]

Susanna is a sound therapist specializing in tuning forks, gong, and singing bowls to restore energetic balance, regulate the nervous system, and support emotional healing. Her work combines somatic and spiritual practices to help clients process stored emotions and navigate chronic pain, anxiety, depression, PTSD, fatigue, and major life transitions. She also facilitates immersive sound baths creating spaces for deep rest, balance, and wellbeing of mind, body, and spirit. She is trained in protocols by Acutonics, Biofield Tuning, Atma Buti School of Vibrational Medicine, and studies gong with Roger Tjoelker and Wayne Marto. Outside her practice, Susanna is a student of herbalism and spends her free time racing gravel bikes and collecting lava lamps.

She infuses each note with pure presence, soul and heartfelt intention to help people feel loved, at peace, and safe to experience the fullness of emotion.

About this Event

Move. Breathe. Regulate.
New York asks a lot of our nervous systems.
We move quickly. We stay connected. We push through. And sometimes we need an intentional space to slow everything down.
Open & Release is a three-hour immersive mind-body experience in Lower Manhattan created to give you that space.
We’ll move.
We’ll breathe.
We’ll reconnect with the body.
And then we’ll give ourselves time to simply be.
Your morning begins with gentle, heart-opening yoga before transitioning into an immersive 9D Breathwork journey. Afterward, we’ll move gently back into the body and close together with a nervous-system regulation circle, grounding tea, light bites, and community.
No prior yoga or breathwork experience is necessary.
Come exactly as you are.

This is not about perfect poses or performance.
It’s about reconnecting with your body.

Certified 9D Breathwork Facilitator Lily Acevedo will guide you through a multi-sensory breathwork journey combining conscious connected breathing with multidimensional audio, music, guided coaching, affirmations, and somatic cues.
Unlike simply listening to a meditation or attending a sound bath, you are actively participating through your breath.
The experience creates an opportunity to slow down, turn inward, explore held tension and emotion, and reconnect with yourself on a deeper level.
There is no “right” experience to have.
Some people notice physical sensations. Some experience emotion or insight. Others experience profound stillness.
Your experience is your own.

This Bijoya, Prabashi Association of Portland brings one of Bengal’s most loved and iconic bands to Portland for an evening filled with the unmistakable wit, nostalgia, melodies, and energy of Chandrabindoo — LIVE!

From songs we grew up listening to, to the quirky lyrics and effortless humor that became their signature, Chandrabindoo has created a musical language entirely their own. Come sing along to the favorites, rediscover old memories, and experience that familiar Chandrabindoo magic with friends and family.

And what better time than Bijoya — when Pujo may be over, but the adda, celebration, and togetherness certainly aren’t.

long_description:
Come join us as we celebrate the biggest festival of the Bengalis.

About this Event

As we step into the 20th year of our Durga Puja, it’s mandatory that we look back and observe many obstacles we have overcome, how we have managed funds, and how we keep organizing the biggest event in our Bengali Culture, mostly how we have become a big joint family. For us, people of BIC, the walls of MM Thompson Room has become the bamboo pandal, the drawings and stuffs made by our decoration team have became the chandelier of Naktala Udayan Sangha, the YouTube Red “dhaak” music has became our real dhaki, sometimes a little snow didn’t stop us to believe that we are enjoying the Sarotkal, like Apu-Durga, we are also chasing though the kaashful and trying to soak up every bit of it. Such power holds this event, such is the power of Maa Durga! অশুভ শক্তির বিনাস, triumph over evil, she make us believe in ourselves, the truth and strength. Every year we bid our Maa Durga farewell with the hope that she’ll bring new virtue within us and she’ll visit us next year.

Halloween puppy yoga is coming to Boston Modern.

Join Kitten Paws and Downward Dogs at Boston Modern Studio in Canton for a gentle, all-levels yoga class with adoptable rescue puppies making the rounds on the mats. title: Monsters of the Mind
description: This month's theme is cognitive distortion,  all the ways our mind creates little monsters. Yoga, therapist guided convos, community.
long_description:
This month's theme is cognitive distortion, all the ways our mind creates little monsters. Yoga, therapist guided convos, community.

About this Event

This is a Mind Body Collective event. The MBC is a social wellness group. We host monthly events that include yoga and diffeerent mental health conversations, guided by their respective professionals. We are a very quickly growing community and would love for you to experience an event with us! This is a space to just show up, try something different, and make new connections.
This month's topic is cognitive distortion. Cognitive distortion is a habitual, often inaccurate pattern of thinking that can cause you to interpret situations, yourself, or the world in a negative or unrealistic way. These thought patterns often happen automatically. They can influence your emotions, behaviors, relationships, and the way you see yourself.
We'll spend about 30 minutes settling into the space, lingering, drinking tea/coffee. Then, an hour long beginner friendly yoga session taught by Chianna Chiem. Followed by a guided group discussion and deep dive into cognitive distortion with Caitlyn Jacquemart, LMFT. And of course, some space and time to linger on the back end.
Co-ed and beginner friendly!

description: A donation-based restorative community yoga practice rooted in nervous system care, gentle movement, connection, and Yoga Nidra.
long_description:
A donation-based restorative community yoga practice rooted in nervous system care, gentle movement, connection, and Yoga Nidra.

About this Event

Yoga for the People is a donation-based community practice created to make movement, nervous system care, and deep rest a little more accessible.
This is not a class about pushing farther, stretching deeper, or performing a perfect pose. We’ll move slowly through restorative and gentle shapes with space to breathe, notice, modify, rest, and listen to what your body is asking for.
We’ll close the practice with Yoga Nidra, an extended guided rest practice that invites you to do something many of us rarely give ourselves permission to do:
nothing.
Come move at your own pace. Come rest. Come breathe. Come be in community without needing to show up as anything other than yourself.
Expect:
• Gentle and restorative yoga
• Breath and nervous system awareness
• Spacious, accessible movement
• Yoga Nidra and guided deep rest
• A welcoming, non-performance-based practice
All levels and bodies are welcome. No previous yoga experience is needed.
Bring a yoga mat, water, and anything cozy you’d like for Yoga Nidra, such as a blanket, sweatshirt, or eye pillow.
This class is donation based. Give what feels accessible to you and come practice with us.

title: Sunday Somatics - Healing with Yoga: Session 2
description: A beginner-friendly yoga series taught by Rhya Moffitt. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.
long_description:
A beginner-friendly yoga series taught by Rhya Moffitt. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.

About this Event

This beginner-friendly yoga series features a heart-centered, healing slow flow practice intimately linked to the Smart's How Do We Heal? 2026-2027 exhibition. Held in the Smart's lobby, the series features gentle movements and contemplative prompts that begin by exploring the various sources of suffering from which we might seek to heal—the physical, emotional, structural, ancestral—then move to methods and practices for healing. This 75-minute class culminates with aromatherapy, breathwork, and contemplative viewing of intentionally selected pieces from the How Do We Heal? collection. Class is led by certified yoga instructor Rhya Moffitt who guides practice with the intention of cultivating inner stillness, awareness, and presence. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.

The first four sessions move through various sources of suffering:
1. physical (health & illness),
2. emotional (loss, grief, and renewal),
3. structural / collective (displacement), and
4. ancestral (trauma)

The last two sessions get into the how with a focus on:
5. wholeness, integration, (mind, body, and spirit) and
6. supportive healing modalities (healing objects).

Free; RSVP encouraged. Limited number of mats available.

Alyssa is an educator, Yin yoga and yoga Nidrā facilitator. She was introduced to yoga Nidrā during a full moon circle at Eaton DC in 2019. long_description:
An intimate candlelit fall experience with cacao, Yin Yoga, restorative sound, reflection, and a tea experience by Rose Glow Tearoom.

About this Event

ROOTED in Rest: A Candlelit Fall Restoration ExperienceAs we transition into fall, nature reminds us that there is a season for slowing down, releasing, and making space for rest.
But in lives that so often ask us to keep moving, working, caring, building, carrying, becoming, rest does not always happen on its own. Sometimes, we have to create space for it intentionally.
ROOTED in Rest is that space.
On Sunday, October 25, Rooting by Nina invites you to an intimate, three-hour candlelit fall restoration experience designed to help you slow down, soften, and simply be.
Limited to just 20 guests, we’ll move intentionally from grounding and gentle movement into deep rest, reflection, nourishment, and connection.

Your experience will includeCeremonial Cacao: beginning our afternoon with intention and grounding
Grounding Breathwork: settling into the body and arriving in the present moment
Yin Yoga + Restorative Sound: slow, supported postures accompanied by sound to invite stillness and release
Immersive Sound Bath: an extended period of rest surrounded by crystal singing bowls and other restorative instruments
Reflective Journaling: space to notice, reflect, and reconnect with yourself
Tea Sommelier Experience featuring Rose Glow Tearoom: a guided, meditative exploration of tea
Tea + Scones: nourishment and an opportunity to linger and connect as we close our afternoon together
You do not need to arrive feeling rested, centered, or even particularly still.
Come exactly as you are.
My hope is that you leave feeling a little more grounded, a little more spacious, and more connected to yourself than when you arrived.
As we enter a season that teaches us so beautifully about transition and release, may we remember that rest is part of the transition, too.

title: stillpoint live @Boston Yoga Union
description: A sound meditation of breath, sound, somatics and stillness...practiced together.
long_description:
A sound meditation of breath, sound, somatics and stillness...practiced together.

About this Event

STILLPOINT LIVE 
Life isn't going to stop being life. What can change is your capacity to meet it.
stillpoint live is a live experience of breath, sound, somatics, and stillness — practiced together, in one room. Not a performance you watch. A practice you do.
Over the course of the evening you'll move through the Stillpoint arc:
Root: arrive, ground, moveBreathe: open, expand, regulateFeel: notice, listen, stay presentRelease: let go of what you're holdingLand: settle, integrate, stillnessIt's a place to practice staying present through sensation, intensity, and emotion, so you leave knowing what presence feels like, and carrying tools for when real life asks the same.
Not escape. Not avoidance. Resilience.
Practice it here. Live it out there.

title: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening
description: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening Classes will guide you through complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual wisdom. An ongoing in-depth course deliving into profound wisdom within Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Hindu/Indian/Vedic spiritual philosophy, and Upanishads. You can see prior recordings at: YesVedanta.com/bg2 Timeless Wisdom of Bhagavad Gita: A Complete Course in Non-Duality in 700 Verses Join us for an in-depth exploration of the Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Vedantic wisdom. Our weekly live Zoom classes will guide you through the complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual knowledge. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue between Krishna (the teacher) and Arjuna (the student), addresses life's deepest questions: What is the nature of the Self? What is the highest purpose of existence? How can one live with intelligence and clarity? If all existence is One, why do we perceive differences? What is the nature of the universe and its origin? How can we understand the cause of the universe? How does one transcend the sense of limitation? This comprehensive study covers: The nature of the Self (Atman) and Reality (Brahman) Self-knowledge that includes dozens of methods to reveal your nature The role of karma, dharma, and free will The nature of the mind and consciousness (or awareness) The art of wise living and decision-making Cultivating emotional maturity and inner peace Through this course, you will: Grasp the core teachings of the Bhagavad Gita and their relevance to modern life Apply practical techniques for refining your thinking and mastering your emotions Develop a deeper understanding of your identity and the world Cultivate inner peace, clarity, and purpose This knowledge offers a step-by-step method to liberate the seeker from the confines of the ego, from the limitations imposed by the material world, and from the cycle of rebirth. description: Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.
long_description:
Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)
Hari Chutney (Fresh Green Chutney)
Sev ka Murabba (Carmelized Cardamom Apples with Pistachio Cream)

Safety & Precautions
At check-in, you will be asked to sign a waiver before entering the Cooking School.

No previous experience is needed, simply get comfortable, close your eyes, and allow yourself to receive. A comfortable yoga bed, pillow, blanket, and bolster will be preset for every participant.

title: Yin and Yoga Nidra
description: A grounding Yin Yoga practice with a guided Yoga Nidra meditation.
long_description:
A grounding Yin Yoga practice with a guided Yoga Nidra meditation.

About this Event

The 90-minute session will combine a grounding Yin Yoga practice with a guided Yoga Nidra meditation.
We’ll begin with approximately 45–50 minutes of Yin Yoga, using longer-held, supported postures designed to encourage relaxation, mobility, and a gradual release of physical tension. The practice will be accessible to a variety of experience levels and will focus on slowing down and settling into the body.
The second portion of the session will transition into Yoga Nidra, a guided relaxation and meditation practice performed while resting comfortably. This portion is intended to support deep rest, nervous system regulation, and mental relaxation.
No previous yoga or meditation experience is required. Participants should wear comfortable clothing and bring a yoga mat. Blankets, pillows, bolsters, or other comfortable props are also encouraged for the Yoga Nidra portion.
The event takes place at Create U., a therapy and integrative wellness collective rooted in creative, embodied healing. Yoga is behind the Create U. house, in the yoga studio/garage.

Join Laura of Soulfish Events, Elyssa of Wolf & Lion, and some of our favorite local partners and vendors for a cosmic Halloween evening at Adams Avenue Fitness.
We’re bringing together movement, music, astrology, community, and a little Halloween magic for a one-of-a-kind AstroYoga silent disco experience. DJ Disco Penny Lane will be spinning live while we move through an all-levels AstroYoga flow, tuning into the energy of the season through movement, music, and connection.
Silent disco headphones will be provided for the class, so you’ll be fully immersed in the music and experience.
And because it’s Halloween weekend, we want you to come dressed as your most out-of-this-world cosmic self. Think celestial, disco, alien, witchy, space cowboy, moon goddess, glam, weird, wonderful. Have fun with it.
Stick around before and after class to connect with our community, meet some of our favorite local wellness partners, and enjoy the evening.

Yoga mat

Your cosmic Halloween look ✨

long_description:
Slow down under the trees with a 75-minute spooky-season yin yoga and meditation practice on the Oasis Lawn.

About this Event

Give yourself permission to slow down, with a little spooky-season energy.
Join us on the Oasis Lawn at Plaza San Antonio Hotel & Spa for Spooky Slow + Still: Yin & Meditation, a 75-minute restorative experience blending long-held yin postures, guided meditation, and intentional stillness in the garden.
Settle into a slower pace as you move through supported poses designed to gently work into the body’s deeper connective tissues, improve mobility and flexibility, and create space to soften rather than strive.
Throughout the practice, moments of meditation and quiet reflection will be woven in, creating a moody, grounding experience inspired by the season. Expect a little candlelight, a little mystery, and plenty of space to breathe, reset, and reconnect.
No previous yoga or meditation experience is needed. You do not need to be flexible or “good” at meditation, just come as you are, get comfortable, and let yourself slow down.

What to BringPlease bring a yoga mat, water, and bug spray. Blocks, bolsters, blankets, or anything else that helps you feel more comfortable are always welcome.

About this Event

The Yoga Club : Friendship Flow at NuLife Fitness CampBring a friend, make a friend, or come as you are! Friendship Flow is a yoga class built for kids and their friends, part of The Yoga Club City Tour. We'll talk about what makes a good friend, then put it into practice with partner games, partner poses, and friendship bracelets to take home - ages 7-11
What kids will learn:
Simple breathing techniques and mindfulness tools they can use anywhere to stay calm, focused, and confident. Each class also explores a life-skills theme. This one is friendship: how to be a good teammate, how to support each other, and how to show up as your best self with the people who matter.
What kids will do:
Start with breathwork and a gentle yoga warm-upJoin a short group discussion on the importance of friendshipMove through partner poses and interactive games that bring the theme to lifeMake a friendship bracelet to share or keepSettle into a mindfulness activity and close with relaxation or guided imageryWhy this class is awesome:
It supports the whole child: body, mind, and friendships. Movement builds strength and flexibility, mindfulness builds focus and emotional regulation, and partner activities strengthen the bonds between friends. Kids leave feeling empowered, balanced, and inspired, with tools to carry into school, home, and every friendship.
What to bring: Comfy clothes and a water bottle. Mats and all materials are provided.
