title: Trauma-Informed Yoga Class for Survivors (November)
description: A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.
long_description:
A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.

About this Event

Cleveland Rape Crisis Center invites survivors of rape and sexual abuse to a free community yoga class. This class is designed to be a safe space for survivors to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. This practice will allow students an opportunity to increase body awareness in support of greater physical, emotional and mental well being.
We will explore breathing practices and therapeutic movement to help survivors in connecting mindfully to the moment. We will learn ways to listen to our bodies and breath so we can honor our own unique experience and needs.

Who can attend?
Survivors of sexual violence/sexual trauma.All yoga experience levels welcome.All genders welcome.Survivors ages 13-17 may attend if accompanied by a parent/guardian. Please register the adult and child separately.

About Dana:
Dana has been practicing and teaching yoga for 20 years. She has trained in a variety of modalities and has learned from many amazing teachers over the years. Her most recent work has been focused on teaching yoga + mindfulness to kids ages K-8, as well as providing Trauma Informed Yoga classes for the community.
“I am deeply committed to this path and am grateful for the opportunity to share all the beautiful healing benefits these practices can provide. Along with my work in schools and as a trauma informed yoga teacher, I am also a mother and musician. I am passionate about creating communities that can support and uplift us all.”

long_description:
Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)

Safety & Precautions

San Diego, this one's for you. Desi Comedy Fest, the biggest South Asian comedy festival in America

About this Event

San Diego, this one's for you. Desi Comedy Fest, the biggest South Asian comedy festival in America, brings its SoCal Tour to the Gaslamp for one night only.
Our mission is simple: showcase the funniest comedians of South Asian heritage from around the globe and create a live comedy experience unlike anything else. Six to eight comedians share one stage, back to back, for two hours of nonstop laughs.
The lineup celebrates the full diversity of the diaspora: Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi, Sri Lankan, Nepali and beyond. From Bollywood to brown parents to growing up between two cultures, this is comedy that hits different when the whole room gets the joke.
And everybody's invited, no translation needed. Featured on NBC, CBS, Just For Laughs and SF Sketchfest, the Fest has sold out rooms across America for over a decade, with comedians who have been part of Netflix Is A Joke, launched specials on Amazon and HBO, and appeared on late night from Letterman to Conan.

As the holiday season approaches, grief can feel especially heavy. Harvest of Healing Retreat II is a compassionate space to pause, reflect, connect, and receive support as we navigate grief and transition into a new season.

• Expert Guidance: Support from therapists, grief coaches, and wellness professionals

• Practical Tools: Strategies and resources to help navigate grief through the holidays and beyond

• Continental breakfast and a light snack

Registration is $50, and space is intentionally limited to help create an intimate and supportive atmosphere.

title: Sunday Somatics - Healing with Yoga: Session 4
description: A beginner-friendly yoga series taught by Rhya Moffitt. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.
long_description:
A beginner-friendly yoga series taught by Rhya Moffitt. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.

About this Event

This beginner-friendly yoga series features a heart-centered, healing slow flow practice intimately linked to the Smart's How Do We Heal? 2026-2027 exhibition. Held in the museum lobby, the series features gentle movements and contemplative prompts that begin by exploring the various sources of suffering from which we might seek to heal—the physical, emotional, structural, ancestral—then move to methods and practices for healing. This 75-minute class culminates with aromatherapy, breathwork, and contemplative viewing of intentionally selected pieces from the How Do We Heal? collection. Class is led by certified yoga instructor Rhya Moffitt who guides practice with the intention of cultivating inner stillness, awareness, and presence. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.

The first four sessions move through various sources of suffering:
1. physical (health & illness),
2. emotional (loss, grief, and renewal),
3. structural / collective (displacement), and
4. ancestral (trauma)

The last two sessions get into the how with a focus on:
5. wholeness, integration, (mind, body, and spirit) and
6. supportive healing modalities (healing objects).

Free; RSVP encouraged. Limited number of mats available.

Learn how to the flavors found in Indian cuisine in your own kitchen. Hands-on. For ages 18+. You’ll work in small teams during class.

About this Event

Age RestrictionsFor ages 18 & up

DescriptionIf you love Indian food and have wondered how to recreate those flavors in your own home, this is the class for you! While the South Asian/Indian culinary diaspora is incredibly diverse, we’re here to lessen the intimidation factor and help you get to know the key spices, knife skills, essential sauces, and cooking methods to get you started.
We’ll pay homage to Madhur Jaffrey, multiple James Beard Award-winner known as the Godmother of Indian Cooking for introducing many people to Indian food in America. Using her approach, we’ll keep class fun, easy, and delicious at every turn. At the end of class everyone will get to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
You will be working in a small group. For ages 18 and up. 21 or older? You’ll enjoy a glass of wine or beer paired with your meal.

MenuLamb Vindaloo
Shahi Murgh (Royal Chicken Cooked in Yogurt)
Massor Dal (Red Lentils Tarka)
Matar Aur Sooay Ka Pullao (Rice with Peas and Dill)
Hari Chutney (Fresh Green Chutney)
Sev ka Murabba (Carmelized Cardamom Apples with Pistachio Cream)

Safety & Precautions
At check-in, you will be asked to sign a waiver before entering the Cooking School.
For that reason, we ask that all attendees arrive at least 5 minutes prior to the confirmed start time of the class.

long_description:
As the season turns, we invite you to slow down, gather, and celebrate the Harvest Season. In Traditional Chinese Medicine, autumn marks a shift inward—a time of gathering, letting go, and conserving our energy as we move toward the stillness of winter. A time to notice what has grown, nourished us, and what we’re ready to carry forward. It's a season of turning inward rather than reaching outward.

The Great Harvest is an evening created around that transition. Held at the iconic Cobblestone Farm in Ann Arbor.

Begin with time to wander through a thoughtfully curated Fall Market, featuring small and local businesses. Browse, shop, and connect with the makers in our community before settling into an autumn-inspired yoga practice with Aubrey + Art. As we move toward the more nourishing, introspective qualities of Yin, our practice will invite you to slow down, soften, listen inward, and create space for what this season has to teach you.

We’ll close the evening around the table with a beautiful Harvest Dinner presented by local private chef Allison Anastasio, celebrating the abundance and flavors of the season. The Great Harvest is an invitation to gather rather than rush, nourish, and celebrate what has already taken root.

description: Body & Soul Art Intensive with Alex Grey & Allyson Grey
long_description:
ABOUT THE PROGRAM

Body & Soul Art Intensive is a creative spiritual practice and visionary ritual intended to turn on the Light Body. Multiple systems of subtle healing life energies run through and surround our body. Seven Chakras, witnessed and reported by clairvoyants as "wheels of light,” ascend the spine and color our emotions and aspirations.

This drawing ritual challenges us to depict the model’s nude presence and encourages us to imagine and portray bio-energetic radiant auras that extend beyond the skin.

WHAT TO EXPECT

Drawing begins on the first morning of the workshop. Each of the seven chakra drawings are briefly introduced by a short guided meditation to consider the energetic force-field associated with the chakra we are about to portray. 

Each participant will create seven drawings focusing on the character and hue of one chakra. Each drawing period is forty-five minutes long, working with meditative focus. The exercise is accompanied by a thematic musical playlist highlighting the archetypal meaning of each chakra. 

To introduce each drawing, a brief blessing describes the meaning, color and vibration of that energy center, identifying specific organs and nerve bundles that correspond within the body. The subject of each drawing is a yogini, a nude model who stands, sits or lies still for class members to draw or paint. 

YOUR INSTRUCTORS

Alex Grey & Allyson Grey

Alex Grey, world-renowned artist, poet, and author, is best loved for his paintings which portray multiple dimensions of reality, interweaving biological anatomy with psychic and spiritual energies. His books, Sacred Mirrors, The Mission of Art, Transfigurations, and Art Psalms, trace the development of his work and mystical experiences that shaped his spiritual artistic life. description: Path to Enlightenment: Live Bhagavad Gita Classes for Spiritual Awakening Classes will guide you through complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual wisdom. An ongoing in-depth course deliving into profound wisdom within Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Hindu/Indian/Vedic spiritual philosophy, and Upanishads. You can see prior recordings at: YesVedanta.com/bg2 Timeless Wisdom of Bhagavad Gita: A Complete Course in Non-Duality in 700 Verses Join us for an in-depth exploration of the Bhagavad Gita, a foundational text of Vedantic wisdom. Our weekly live Zoom classes will guide you through the complexities of life and reveal your true nature through the highest spiritual knowledge. The Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue between Krishna (the teacher) and Arjuna (the student), addresses life's deepest questions: What is the nature of the Self? What is the highest purpose of existence? long_description:
Get ready to dance the night away with silent beats from Bollywood to Tollywood and all the cool vibes underneath the stary night!

About this Event

Headphones on, Austin. Bollywood, Tollywood and everything in between, at The Domain, Amy Donovan Plaza.
Overview
When the sun goes down on Panchabhootam, the plaza turns into a dance floor.
Join SAIVA on Saturday, November 14, from 8:30 to 9:30 PM for a silent disco at The Domain's Amy Donovan Plaza. Bollywood, Tollywood, and everything in between, playing straight into your headphones under the open Texas sky.
This is the closing celebration of Panchabhootam, SAIVA's festival of the five great elements: earth, water, fire, air and space. All afternoon, the elements come alive through the senses. The silent disco ends the day with sound, the sense of space, and everyone dancing together.
At SAIVA, we believe every generation has something to give and something to learn. So bring your grandmother, your kids, your college roommate and your neighbors. Some of our best dancers have been practicing in our weekly classes since May.
How it works
When you arrive, you'll pick up a pair of wireless headphones. 3 channels each play a different mix, and the light on your headset shows which one you're tuned to, so you can find the people dancing to your song.
Want to talk? Slide one ear off. No shouting over speakers, and no ringing ears on the drive home. It's the most social way to dance.
Make a day of it
Come early for the free Panchabhootam festival from 3 to 6 PM at the same plaza:

About this Event

The Sleep Reset: Release with lymphatic drainage. Nourish your changing body. Rituals that help you sleep.It is 3 a.m. You are wide awake, running tomorrow's to-do list, and everyone else in the house is asleep. If that is your night, this evening is for you.
Sleep is one of the most common struggles for moms, and nobody hands you a plan for it. So we built one.
This is a hands-on evening, and you will practice everything in the room before you go home.

title: Sip & Flow: Mom Edition
description: Start with yoga, end with wine.
long_description:
Start with yoga, end with wine.

About this Event

Mama, this afternoon is yours.
Leave the babies, the husbands, and the never-ending laundry at home. They'll all be right where you left them (especially the laundry). For three hours, you get to show up as yourself, with nobody asking for a snack.
We'll start on the mat with a flow designed for bodies that carry, lift, rock, and chase all day long. Expect gentle strength, deep stretches for tired hips, shoulders, and backs, and plenty of room to breathe. Every level is welcome, whether you practice weekly or haven't unrolled a mat since before the kids.
Then we sip. You'll enjoy a guided tasting of three wines from mom-owned wineries, poured alongside the stories of the women who make them. These are mothers who know the juggle and still found a way to build something beautiful, and their wines are sure to inspire. Non-alcoholic options are available so every mama has a glass in hand.
And woven through it all: conversation with women who get it. The sleepless nights, the bedtime negotiations, the mental load, and the wins nobody else noticed. Come to share, laugh, vent, or simply sit back with your glass and soak it in.
Your ticket includes:
A recharging yoga flow for moms at every stageA guided flight of three mom-owned winesLight bitesReal community with women in your season of lifeLeisure is a right, not a reward, and mamas have more than earned theirs. Grab your ticket, grab a friend, and come recharge with us.

title: Special Program: Counter-Histories—Memory, Materiality & South Asian Art
description: Syona Puliady and UCLA Arts Dean Lionel Popkin discuss South Asian art, material, memory, and reimagined histories.
long_description:
Syona Puliady and UCLA Arts Dean Lionel Popkin discuss South Asian art, material, memory, and reimagined histories.

About this Event

Curator of Textiles of the Eastern Hemisphere Syona Puliady will join UCLA Dean of the School of the Arts and Architecture Lionel Popkin for a conversation on the themes underlying Textiles as Monument and Field Notes from Begumpura: memory, materiality, and the creation of alternative histories through contemporary art.

By focusing on the works of Suchitra Mattai, Jagdeep Raina, Swapnaa Tamhane, and Rahee Punyashloka, Puliady and Popkin will consider how artists use textiles, speculative storytelling, archival practices, and other forms of cultural expression to challenge dominant narratives and center communities whose histories have often been overlooked. Together, they will address how contemporary South Asian artists create new forms of remembrance, belonging, and possibility through material and imagined worlds.

Lionel Popkin is the dean of the UCLA School of the Arts and Architecture and a professor of choreography in the UCLA Department of World Arts and Cultures/Dance. He previously served as the school’s associate dean for academic affairs (2021–24) and chair of the World Arts and Cultures/Dance department (2015–18). Popkin’s artistic practice engages people, objects, and media to explore hybridity, archival practices, and the complexities of representing the South Asian diaspora in North America. His performance and video artworks have been presented at leading cultural venues on four continents, and his written works have been included in scholarly journals and arts publications. He joined UCLA's faculty in 2006 and is a resident artist at the 18th Street Arts Center.

long_description:
Join us for a unique outdoor yoga experience that combines beginner friendly yoga, fresh air, laughter, and plenty of goat interaction. Whether you’re coming with friends, family, coworkers, or just looking for a fun and memorable outing, goat yoga is designed to be relaxed and enjoyable for all experience levels.

Please dress appropriately for the weather, as this is an outdoor event.

For safety reasons, children under the age of 5 are not permitted inside the fenced goat yoga participation area at any time, including as observers or accompanying guests.

Know Before You Go:

• Please do not enter the fenced goat yoga area earlier than 15 minutes before your scheduled class time. We’ll leave extra time after class for photos and socializing with the goats.

• BYOM (Bring Your Own Mat) — We do not provide yoga mats, but large towels will be available for all attendees. We also provide bottled water, sunscreen, bug spray, hand sanitizer, and wipes.

• Be prepared for our goats to take an interest in you! Goat yoga is designed to be lighthearted and interactive. Our goats may nudge, nibble, scratch, jump, or step on guests during class. Children ages 5+ are welcome with a participating parent or guardian.

• Most of our goats are Nigerian Dwarf goats and are generally under 25 pounds, though some of our larger personalities can occasionally reach 30–35 pounds.

• Our goats are not potty trained animals. While we do our best to keep the space clean throughout the session, occasional droppings are a normal and expected part of the experience. Sanitizing stations and antibacterial wipes will be available.

• All attendees must check in and complete a provided liability waiver prior to class. Masks are not required. Social distancing and personal comfort levels regarding proximity to others are left to each attendee’s discretion.

Our tribe looks forward to meeting you!

title: Trauma-Informed Yoga Class for Survivors (December)
description: A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.
long_description:
A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.

About this Event

Cleveland Rape Crisis Center invites survivors of rape and sexual abuse to a free community yoga class. This class is designed to be a safe space for survivors to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. This practice will allow students an opportunity to increase body awareness in support of greater physical, emotional and mental well being.
We will explore breathing practices and therapeutic movement to help survivors in connecting mindfully to the moment. We will learn ways to listen to our bodies and breath so we can honor our own unique experience and needs.

Who can attend?
Survivors of sexual violence/sexual trauma.All yoga experience levels welcome.All genders welcome.Survivors ages 13-17 may attend if accompanied by a parent/guardian. Please register the adult and child separately.

About Dana:
Dana has been practicing and teaching yoga for 20 years. She has trained in a variety of modalities and has learned from many amazing teachers over the years. About this Event

Puppy yoga comes to Windy Hill — and every ticket helps rescue puppies find homes.
Join Kitten Paws and Downward Dogs at Windy Hill Athletic Club on Saturday, December 5 for 45 minutes of gentle, all-levels yoga surrounded by adoptable puppies from a local Atlanta rescue partner. Flow, stretch, get climbed on, and take as many puppy breaks as you need. Nobody minds.
The puppies are the point. Every puppy in the room is a rescue and is looking for a home. Our rescue partner brings the puppies, their pen and their volunteers, so you can meet, cuddle and start an adoption conversation on the spot. We'll name the rescue here as soon as they're confirmed.
Where the money goes. Net proceeds go straight to the rescue, scaled to seats sold. The more of you who show up, the bigger the check.
THE DAY
• Saturday, December 5, 2026 · Session 2: class 1:00–1:45 PM (Session 1 runs 12:00–12:45 PM on a separate ticket)
• Windy Hill Athletic Club · 135 Interstate North Parkway SE, Atlanta, GA 30339
• Yoga led by one of Windy Hill Athletic Club's own instructors · all levels welcome, including complete beginners
• Wear something you don't mind a puppy paw on
GOOD TO KNOW
• Tickets are limited to keep the puppy-to-person ratio happy. When it's sold out, it's sold out.
• Tickets are non-refundable but fully transferable — send a friend in your place.
• Real puppies: expect a little chaos, a little noise and a lot of joy. The rescue's volunteers handle everything the puppies do.
About Kitten Paws and Downward Dogs
We are a 501(c)(3) that produces puppy events with adoptable animals from rescues and shelters only — never breeders. Across 100+ events we have raised $145,000+ for animal rescues. kittenpawsdownwarddogs.org

About this Event

Come flow with us to benefit Give Like a Mother. Give Like A Mother (GLAM) is a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that local children and teens in need have access to seasonally appropriate clothing.
Though we operate on donations of gently used items, we are committed to providing high-quality, in-style clothing that kids can wear with confidence. When children feel good about what they’re wearing, it can boost their self-worth, reduce the risk of ridicule, and ultimately support their success in school and beyond.
Our name may be fun and a little sassy, but it carries a serious challenge. Mothers give everything they can for their children—yet sometimes, even that isn’t enough.
That’s why we’re asking you: Will you Give Like A Mother and help a child in need?
100% of all donations go directly to the charity. We thank Fretboard Brewing for donating the space and Anissa Dowling for donating her time and talent in leading the yoga class that is always fun and perfect for all levels.
Bring a friend and enjoy $1 off beers in the tap room after class!

long_description:

long_description:
Kick off the weekend with Susanna Barkataki. 

Yoga is much more than poses.

At its roots, yoga is a structured, living ethical system, a practical, radical, and deeply compassionate framework for how to be in the world. And when we actually live it, our lives completely change.

This immersive morning session goes deep into the heart of yogic philosophy: Susanna will share stories from her life, the Yamas and Niyamas, Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, and the full Eightfold Path as a path to embody, practice and breathe into your actual life.

Through practice, reflection, discussion, and direct transmission, we explore:

Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha the five outer ethical codes and how they guide us in relationship, teaching, and community

Saucha, Santosha, Tapas, Svadhyaya, Ishvara Pranidhana the five inner codes for soulful, engaged living

The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali including the Locks and Keys of Sutra 1.33, and how "Yogas Chitta Vritti Nirodhah" is not an idea but an experience

How yogic ethics are a framework for justice, equity, and liberation not just personal transformation

How to bring these teachings authentically into your cuing, your sequencing, and your studio culture

Expect to move, reflect, discuss, and go home with practices you can use immediately in your teaching, your relationships, and your daily life.

CEUs available.

long_description: The BMW Dallas Marathon has been a Texas running tradition for over 40 years. The race weekend features a full marathon, half marathon, ultra marathon, 5-person relay, 10K, and 5K — something for every runner. The course starts at Dallas City Hall, loops through scenic White Rock Lake, and finishes back downtown. Since 1997, the marathon has donated nearly $5 million to Scottish Rite for Children. title: Trauma-Informed Roots of Yoga: Healing the Nervous System, Honoring the Tradition
venue_name: 2758 Wyoming Street, 1st Floor , St. Louis, MO, United States, Missouri 63118
description:
Yoga was always a healing practice. The tradition has known what modern neuroscience is only beginning to name: that the body holds what the mind cannot yet speak, and that breath, movement, sound, and community can bring us home to ourselves.

This closing session brings together the wisdom of trau
long_description:
Yoga was always a healing practice. The tradition has known what modern neuroscience is only beginning to name: that the body holds what the mind cannot yet speak, and that breath, movement, sound, and community can bring us home to ourselves.

This closing session brings together the wisdom of trauma-informed teaching, somatic experiencing, and yogic philosophy to explore how we practice and teach yoga in a way that genuinely heals and how we reckon honestly with the ways yoga spaces can also cause harm.

Susanna guides you through an embodied, grounded exploration of:

The physiology of trauma what happens in the brain, nervous system, and body, and what yoga uniquely offers for each stress response state

Colonial and racial trauma how systemic oppression lives in the body, and how it is woven into the history of yoga itself

Trauma-informed, culturally competent language and cueing what to say, what not to say, and how to create brave, accessible, genuinely inclusive spaces

Yogic resources for healing pranayama, grounding, orienting, mantra, and somatic practices drawn directly from the tradition's own roots

Community care and teacher self-care "Nobody can do it for us. And we can't do it alone." 

We end where the weekend began: in practice. In breath. In the recognition that yoga, at its deepest roots, has always been a technology for liberation personal and collective, ancient and urgently needed right now. 

CEUs available. 

Early bird pricing available until 10/31/26.

long_description:
Dive into Winter Solstice magic with Tej Ray! Candlelit music, Yoga Nidra, breathwork sound healing for deep renewal. Join the enchantment!

About this Event

The Winter Solstice marks the longest night of the year—a sacred turning point where we pause, exhale, and return to the quiet center within. It is a time of stillness, dreaming, and deep restoration.
Join Tej and Ray for a candlelit journey into the heart of winter. Through original music, guided Yoga Nidra, breathwork, and immersive sound healing, you’ll be held in a space of warmth, wonder, and renewal.
The Journey Includes:
🌅 Original songs by Ray to open and close the ceremony
💫 Seasonal astrology update + guided Yoga Nidra by Tej
🎶 Live music, poetry, and moments of deep stillness
🌬 Breathwork to soothe the nervous system and settle the body
🌀 Meditation journey with kaleidoscope visuals, crystal bowls, djembe, and gong
🎼 Full sound healing immersion while resting in stillness
🌙 Closing intention ritual and shared resonance to carry forward
🧺 What to Bring:
Yoga mat + cozy layers
Blanket, bolster, pillow, or anything for deep comfort
Optional eye cover or journal
Water bottle
Pre-registration encouraged | Space is limited

description: Experience the Vibrance of Tamil Culture at the San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
long_description:
Experience the Vibrance of Tamil Culture at the San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
Mark your calendars for December 31st, 2026, as on this day, the San Diego Tamil Sangam will host its highly anticipated Annual Membership event. A cultural extravaganza that celebrates the richness and diversity of Tamil heritage, this event is a golden opportunity for Tamil enthusiasts to come together and revel in the vibrancy of this ancient culture. The event is sure to be a hub of engagement, enrichment, and entertainment that fosters the promotion and preservation of Tamil language, arts, and literature.
Artist: A Secret Yet to be Revealed
The event is yet to announce its artist, but it's known for featuring renowned individuals from the Tamil community who have significantly influenced the preservation and promotion of Tamil culture. The mystery guest, no doubt, will offer a memorable experience, showcasing the beauty of Tamil arts and literature that resonates with the audience and deepens their appreciation for this rich culture.
Immerse Yourself in Tamil Culture in the Heart of San Diego
The event takes place in San Diego, California, specifically at the 750 B Street location. The venue is in an easily accessible area of the city, known for its safety and proximity to a variety of attractions. After the event, guests can explore the city's vibrant nightlife, historical landmarks, and breathtaking beaches. And for those craving authentic Indian cuisine, there are numerous Indian restaurants nearby where you can indulge in a variety of flavorful dishes.
Secure Your Membership: Ticket Information
Various membership options are available for purchase, ensuring there's something for everyone. The Annual Family Membership is priced at $60.00, providing an excellent opportunity for families to be part of the Tamil community in San Diego. The Annual Individual Membership is available for $35.00, perfect for individuals passionate about Tamil culture. Additionally, the Student Membership from India is priced at a discounted rate of $10.00. For those who want to make a long-term commitment, the Lifetime Membership is available for $500.00. Make sure to secure your membership and be part of the San Diego Tamil Sangam's thriving community.

Learn asana alignment for your body, develop personal meditation and pranayama practices, learn the fundamentals of Ayurveda and how to create and sequence a home, whole-body practice for your health and well-being.

Modules include Asana: Standing and Seated, Backbends, Twists, Arm Balances, Inversions and Sun Salutations; Ayurveda; Meditation; Pranayama and creating a personalized home practice. Classes run Thursday evenings, 6:00-8:30 pm January 7th through May 20th. Limited to 10 students.

long_description:
Usama Siddiquee is a Bengali-American stand-up comedian, writer, and actor based in New York City. He is currently a finalist on Kevin Hart’s Funny AF for Netflix, which premiered on April 20. In 2024, he made his late-night debut on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, and in 2025 released his first half-hour special with Don’t Tell Comedy on YouTube. The special highlights his signature high-energy, rapid-fire style, with material ranging from growing up Muslim in Texas to dating misadventures and even getting kicked off America’s Got Talent.

As an actor, Usama has appeared in Netflix’s Inventing Anna and Survival of the Thickest, HBO’s And Just Like That, Comedy Central’s Awkwafina Is Nora from Queens, and FX’s Better Things. He recently wrapped a supporting role in the upcoming Netflix comedy Best of the Best, alongside Hasan Minhaj, Priyanka Kedia, and Maitreyi Ramakrishnan.

Usama was named a New Face at the prestigious Just For Laughs Festival in 2018. In 2020, he reached the semifinals of America’s Got Talent and appeared in the ABC Discovers Talent Showcase. A decorated festival performer, he was a finalist in the 2017 New York’s Funniest competition at Caroline’s and the NBC Stand-Up competition, and has won top honors at the Laughing Devil Cup Comedy Festival (2016), Yonkers Comedy Festival (2015), and Make Me Laugh Albany Comedy Festival (2015). His work has also been featured by NBC, BuzzFeed, Refinery29, The Scene, Mic.com, FusionTV, and The Huffington Post.

description: Ready to deepen your practice and become a more confident, skillful teacher?
long_description:
Ready to deepen your practice and become a more confident, skillful teacher?

About this Event

Rocket Yoga 30hrs Teacher TrainingJoin licensed Rocket Yoga Trainer Andre for an immersive 30-hour teacher training designed to help you elevate both your personal practice and your teaching. Through daily Rocket classes, technical workshops, hands-on coaching, and the signature Misfits Method, you'll gain practical tools you can immediately apply in the classroom.

Whether you teach Rocket, Vinyasa, or Ashtanga, this training will challenge your body, expand your perspective, and refine your teaching.

What You'll Learn

Throughout the training, you'll explore:

•⁠ ⁠Rocket I, II, III & Rocket BBQ
•⁠ ⁠Classic and hybrid Rocket sequences
•⁠ ⁠Intelligent assists and adjustments
•⁠ ⁠Pose breakdowns and movement mechanics
•⁠ ⁠Drills to build strength, mobility, and confidence
•⁠ ⁠Transitions and arm balance progressions
•⁠ ⁠Creative sequencing
•⁠ ⁠Teaching methodology rooted in the Misfits Method
•⁠ ⁠How to support students with playfulness, strength, and ease

The Misfits Method is built on the belief that students learn best when they're challenged, supported, and encouraged to explore. While the training is rooted in Rocket Yoga, the techniques and teaching skills you'll develop are equally valuable for Vinyasa and Ashtanga instructors.

Come ready to honor the lineage, bend the rules, and expand what's possible.

Who Is This Training For?

This training is ideal for:

•⁠ ⁠Certified yoga teachers looking to expand their teaching toolkit
•⁠ ⁠Rocket Yoga practitioners ready to deepen their understanding
•⁠ ⁠Vinyasa and Ashtanga teachers wanting to improve their cueing, adjustments, and sequencing
•⁠ ⁠Dedicated students looking to take their practice to the next level

Join our watch list for updates for

Musicians: MC YOGI Benjy + Heather Wertheimer

Join us in San Francisco for a transformative yoga gathering designed to support well-being, deepen self-awareness, and cultivate resilience in an ever-changing world. More than a conference, this experience is a journey of personal transformation, collective connection, and conscious living.
Led by a diverse faculty of visionary teachers and wellness practitioners, this immersive gathering weaves together the enduring teachings of yoga with contemporary tools for embodied, balanced living. Participants will explore a wide range of integrative practices—including asana, pranayama, meditation, philosophy, Yoga Nidra, Ayurveda, sound healing, yoga for recovery and nervous system support—to build a comprehensive tool-kit for life both on and off the mat.
Whether you’re a lifelong student or a seasoned teacher, this gathering offers a rare opportunity to pause, reflect, and reconnect—with your body, your breath, your community, and the Earth. In a world that moves fast, this is your invitation to slow down and remember what truly matters.
